title: A shared registry conversation for SHOC2 and RAF1 families

sentences.text: As a RASopathies Network leader, I invite Noonan Syndrome Association (UK) to explore collaboration for families affected by SHOC2-related disorders (Mazzanti syndrome).
The atlas infers your RAF1 community connection; your website describes Noonan syndrome support without naming RAF1.
SHOC2 and some RAF1 changes make proteins overactive, and both genes participate in MAPK cell signalling.
Their symptom similarity is atlas-inferred, with confidence 0.43—below 0.5—not proof that families have identical needs.

sections.heading: What already exists that we could share

sentences.text: PATRAS (EURAS) and our contact registry are possible starting points, although their SHOC2 coverage is atlas-inferred and the contact registry page describes it as being built.
The Clinical, Genetic, and Epidemiologic Study of Children and Adults With RASopathies explicitly includes SHOC2; its connection to RAS-CM is atlas-inferred.
The RASopathy Biorepository is another potential resource to adapt, with RAF1 coverage inferred by the atlas.

sections.heading: What must be checked before we join forces

sentences.text: Please help check whether loose anagen hair, myelofibrosis and duplicated collecting system occur in RAF1 families rather than assuming missing records mean absence.
For adaptable resources, check loose anagen hair, myelofibrosis and the five additional, unspecified symptom gaps flagged in the input.
Confirm study eligibility, any required eligibility changes, and each variant’s effect before extending participation.
RAF1 variants can increase or impair protein activity, so a single overactivity label is insufficient.
Let us hold one short joint review of a draft PATRAS invitation for RAF1 families, making any offer conditional on confirmation of registry eligibility.
Is any interventional study open specifically to SHOC2-, CBL- or HRAS-related disorders?
Which individual variants are activating, catalytically impaired—working less effectively—or loss of function?
Dear Noonan Syndrome Association (UK),
Could we explore a small registry collaboration for SHOC2 and RAF1 families?
PATRAS offers a starting point, but its SHOC2 connection is atlas-inferred.
Would you review a draft family invitation with us this month?
Let us confirm eligibility and symptom coverage before sharing it.
Thank you for considering this invitation.
[Your name], on behalf of RASopathies Network (RASopathiesNet USA / UK)
